<body>
<article class="spectraa-deep-dive">
  <header class="topbar"><span class="brand">AETHOS WEALTH · IPO DEEP DIVE</span><span>SPECTRAA TECHNOLOGY SOLUTIONS</span></header>
  <div class="hero">
    <div class="eyebrow">Aethos Wealth · IPO Deep Dive</div>
    <h1>SpectraA Technology Solutions Limited</h1>
    <p class="deck">A 17-year process-plant engineer entering the public market with strong FY26 margins, a ₹81 crore order book and a Jaipur expansion that more than doubles factory floor area.</p>
    <div class="callout"><strong>The central question:</strong> Is SpectraA building a repeatable engineering platform with defensible process know-how—or is the IPO extrapolating one strong year before output capacity, utilisation and customer identities are adequately disclosed?</div>
    <div class="stats">
      <div class="stat"><strong>₹42.52 Cr</strong><span>Total offer at ₹118</span></div>
      <div class="stat"><strong>₹157.5 Cr</strong><span>Post-issue market cap</span></div>
      <div class="stat"><strong>13.6x</strong><span>Post-money FY26 P/E</span></div>
      <div class="stat"><strong>₹81.30 Cr</strong><span>Order book: 25 Aug 2026</span></div>
    </div>
    <div class="image-row"><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Copper distillation equipment"><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Industrial process installation"><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="SpectraA manufacturing facility"></div>
    <h3>Research stance</h3>
    <p>SpectraA has credible end-to-end process-plant capability, a broad stainless-steel and copper equipment portfolio, rising repeat-customer revenue, export momentum and strong FY26 profitability. The counterweight is customer opacity, working-capital intensity, supplier-funded cash conversion, regulatory clean-up around IPO readiness and a floor-area-led expansion without quantified output capacity.</p>
    <p class="fineprint"><strong>Document basis:</strong> Red Herring Prospectus dated September 10, 2026. Offer parameters are evaluated at the ₹118 cap price. All product and factory images are reproduced from the RHP.</p>
  </div>

  <main>
    <section id="business">
      <p class="section-kicker">Company overview</p><h2>1. Business architecture and opportunity</h2>
      <div class="callout green"><strong>What SpectraA sells:</strong> engineered process plants and equipment—from design and fabrication through installation, commissioning, operator training and after-sales support—for breweries, distilleries, malt spirit, food and beverage, extraction and allied process industries.</div>
      <div class="flow"><div><strong>Design</strong><span>CAD/CAE, P&amp;ID, BOM</span></div><div><strong>Fabricate</strong><span>SS/copper, weld, polish</span></div><div><strong>Validate</strong><span>NDT, pressure test, FAT</span></div><div><strong>Deliver</strong><span>Install, commission, train</span></div></div>
      <div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>FY26 product segment</th><th>Revenue</th><th>Share</th><th>Primary use case</th></tr></thead><tbody>
        <tr><td>Commercial brewery equipment</td><td>₹68.93 Cr</td><td>68.14%</td><td>Industrial brewing, fermentation, storage, CIP and filtration</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Distillery equipment</td><td>₹11.80 Cr</td><td>11.66%</td><td>Copper pot stills and spirit distillation systems</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Malt spirit equipment</td><td>₹10.40 Cr</td><td>10.28%</td><td>Milling, mashing, fermentation and distillation</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Microbrewery equipment</td><td>₹8.58 Cr</td><td>8.48%</td><td>Smaller craft-brewing plants and cellar systems</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Extraction / F&amp;B / others</td><td>₹1.45 Cr</td><td>1.44%</td><td>Botanical extraction, blending and thermal processing</td></tr>
      </tbody></table></div>
      <h3>Industry and demand drivers</h3><ul><li>Brewers and distillers require hygienic, traceable and process-consistent systems; greenfield projects and brownfield debottlenecking support demand.</li><li>Customer economics depend on yield, batch consistency, cleaning time, energy use and uptime. Equipment qualification and commissioning history matter more than the steel vessel alone.</li><li>The opportunity is attractive but project-led and cyclical. SpectraA has not disclosed its market share, while larger competitors have deeper balance sheets and broader service networks.</li></ul>
    </section>

    <section id="products">
      <p class="section-kicker">What the company builds</p><h2>2. Products, use cases and process technology</h2>
      <div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Product family</th><th>Equipment / technology</th><th>Customer outcome</th></tr></thead><tbody>
        <tr><td>Commercial &amp; craft brewing</td><td>Brewhouse and cellar vessels; mash/wort kettles, lauter tun, whirlpool, fermenters, unitanks, bright-beer tanks, filtration and CIP</td><td>Controlled brewing, fermentation, cleaning and storage</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Distillery</td><td>3,000–24,000 L copper pot stills; radiators, reboilers or coils; programmed automatic spirit distillation</td><td>Vapour-contact geometry and thermal control influence spirit character and repeatability</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Malt spirit</td><td>Milling, mashing, fermentation, copper wash/spirit stills, condensers, blending and storage</td><td>Integrated line from grain processing to spirit handling</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Food &amp; beverage</td><td>CSD blending, flash pasteurisation and carbo-blending; pulp, jam, ketchup, juice and energy-drink systems</td><td>Hygienic mixing, thermal treatment and dosing</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Extraction</td><td>Solvent-based extractors and holding/buffer tanks for chilli, turmeric, marigold and spices</td><td>Recovery of botanical colours, flavours and actives</td></tr>
      </tbody></table></div>
      <h3>Specific engineering stack</h3><ul><li><strong>Design:</strong> CAD/CAE, P&amp;IDs, product lifecycle/version control, bills of material and reusable software/control blocks.</li><li><strong>Fabrication:</strong> AISI 304/304L and 316/316L stainless steel plus copper; CNC/plasma cutting, rolling, welding, automatic polishing, passivation, electropolishing, insulation and cladding.</li><li><strong>Heat transfer &amp; cleaning:</strong> Omega laser-welded jackets, dimple jackets/pillow plates and clean-in-place systems.</li><li><strong>Quality:</strong> WPS/PQR, qualified welders, argon-purged sanitary welds, heat/batch traceability, DPT/RT/UT/MPI, pressure/leak testing and pre-FAT/FAT.</li><li><strong>Large-vessel execution:</strong> on-site fabrication where transportation limits factory-built delivery.</li></ul>
      <div class="callout amber"><strong>Disclosure strength:</strong> the RHP states 100% FAT success and no warranty claims in the last three fiscal years and the period ended September 30, 2025. Sample size, test protocol and claim thresholds are not disclosed.</div>
    </section>

    <section id="gallery">
      <p class="section-kicker">Actual RHP photographs</p><h2>3. Product gallery</h2>
      <div class="gallery">
        <figure><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Stainless process vessel"><figcaption>Stainless process vessel</figcaption></figure>
        <figure><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Dimple-jacket vessel"><figcaption>Dimple-jacket vessel</figcaption></figure>
        <figure><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Copper distillation system"><figcaption>Copper distillation system</figcaption></figure>
        <figure><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Bottling and process line"><figcaption>Bottling / process line</figcaption></figure>
        <figure><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Packaged process skid"><figcaption>Packaged process skid</figcaption></figure>
        <figure><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Microbrewery cellar"><figcaption>Microbrewery cellar</figcaption></figure>
        <figure><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Copper still installation"><figcaption>Copper still installation</figcaption></figure>
        <figure><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Industrial process plant"><figcaption>Industrial process plant</figcaption></figure>
      </div>
      <div class="callout"><strong>Investor read-through:</strong> the photographs support real fabrication and installation capability across stainless-steel vessels, copper distillation systems and integrated skids. They do not, by themselves, establish proprietary IP or capacity utilisation.</div>
      <h3>Turnkey versus non-turnkey revenue</h3><div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>₹ crore</th><th>FY24</th><th>FY25</th><th>FY26</th><th>FY26 mix</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Turnkey projects</td><td>81.59</td><td>64.37</td><td>87.78</td><td>86.77%</td></tr><tr><td>Non-turnkey supply</td><td>7.37</td><td>10.79</td><td>13.38</td><td>13.23%</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
      <p class="fineprint">Turnkey work increases wallet share and embeds engineering responsibility, but typically carries milestone billing, site execution and collection risk.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="moat">
      <p class="section-kicker">Entry barriers</p><h2>4. Competitive moat—what is real, what is not</h2>
      <div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Moat element</th><th>Evidence</th><th>Replicability / assessment</th></tr></thead><tbody>
        <tr><td>End-to-end execution</td><td>Design, fabrication, controls, installation, commissioning, training and service</td><td>Meaningful for smaller challengers; requires coordinated teams and references</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Engineering library</td><td>Accumulated P&amp;IDs, drawings, BOMs and reusable controls across 17 years</td><td>Learning-curve advantage, but no quantified proprietary library or software ownership disclosed</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Hygienic fabrication</td><td>Sanitary welds, traceability, NDT, pressure testing and FAT</td><td>A qualification barrier; established fabricators can replicate with investment and discipline</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Copper-still know-how</td><td>Geometry and thermal configuration for spirit distillation</td><td>Application know-how matters; patents are not disclosed</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Installed references &amp; service</td><td>50+ clients, operator training, spares, O&amp;M and AMC</td><td>Reduces perceived execution risk and supports repeat orders</td></tr>
        <tr><td>ISO 9001:2015</td><td>TÜV Rheinland; valid to 14 Sep 2027; broad operational scope</td><td>Credibility and audit hygiene—not unique differentiation</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Paques collaboration</td><td>Wastewater/biogas know-how and support agreement dated 31 Aug 2025</td><td>Broadens solutions; exclusivity is not disclosed</td></tr>
      </tbody></table></div>
      <div class="callout red"><strong>Moat verdict:</strong> SpectraA has an execution moat, not a patent moat. Only a word trademark is disclosed; no patent portfolio, ASME/PED certification or exclusive core process licence is identified in the RHP. Praj, Alfa Laval and GEA remain credible competitive references.</div>
      <h3>What would strengthen the moat claim</h3><ul><li>Customer-approved vendor status, tender win rates and repeat-project chronology by segment.</li><li>Measured yield, energy, water, cleaning-time and commissioning advantages.</li><li>More third-party certifications, proprietary automation modules or protected process designs.</li><li>A growing AMC/O&amp;M installed base with recurring service revenue separately disclosed.</li></ul>
    </section>

    <section id="customers">
      <p class="section-kicker">Commercial quality</p><h2>5. Customers, concentration and attrition</h2>
      <div class="stats"><div class="stat"><strong>15.01%</strong><span>Largest customer: FY26</span></div><div class="stat"><strong>46.75%</strong><span>Top 5 customers</span></div><div class="stat"><strong>65.60%</strong><span>Top 10 customers</span></div><div class="stat"><strong>50.07%</strong><span>Repeat-order revenue</span></div></div>
      <div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Metric</th><th>FY24</th><th>FY25</th><th>FY26</th><th>Interpretation</th></tr></thead><tbody>
        <tr><td>Top 1 customer</td><td>16.34%</td><td>11.50%</td><td>15.01%</td><td>Largest account rose again in FY26</td></tr><tr><td>Top 3 customers</td><td>42.83%</td><td>34.62%</td><td>35.18%</td><td>More than one-third of revenue</td></tr><tr><td>Top 5 customers</td><td>52.60%</td><td>44.60%</td><td>46.75%</td><td>Material project concentration</td></tr><tr><td>Top 10 customers</td><td>72.37%</td><td>61.91%</td><td>65.60%</td><td>Improved versus FY24, worsened versus FY25</td></tr><tr><td>Repeat-order revenue</td><td>38.87%</td><td>30.68%</td><td>50.07%</td><td>Strong rebound; revenue measure only</td></tr><tr><td>New-customer revenue</td><td>61.13%</td><td>69.32%</td><td>49.93%</td><td>New wins still contribute about half</td></tr>
      </tbody></table></div>
      <div class="callout amber"><strong>Customer names are not disclosed.</strong> The company states that names are confidential and consents were not received. Investors cannot independently evaluate the quality, credit profile or longevity of the largest accounts from the RHP.</div>
      <h3>Client attrition—do not confuse the proxy with churn</h3><ul><li><strong>Customer-count attrition, customers lost, GRR and NRR are not disclosed.</strong></li><li>Repeat-order revenue of 50.07% is a project-revenue mix, not a retention rate.</li><li>No significant customer reportedly failed its obligations during FY24–FY26. That is a credit statement, not evidence of zero attrition.</li><li>No major order cancellations were reported over the last three fiscals, although quantities and prices were modified.</li></ul>
    </section>

    <section id="orderbook">
      <p class="section-kicker">Pipeline quality</p><h2>6. Order book, exports and revenue visibility</h2>
      <div class="stats"><div class="stat"><strong>₹81.30 Cr</strong><span>Order book: 25 Aug 2026</span></div><div class="stat"><strong>0.80x</strong><span>Order book / FY26 revenue</span></div><div class="stat"><strong>29.38%</strong><span>FY26 export share</span></div><div class="stat"><strong>56.32%</strong><span>International share of Mar-26 book</span></div></div>
      <div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>FY26 export geography</th><th>Revenue</th><th>Share of exports</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Germany</td><td>₹15.19 Cr</td><td>51.09%</td></tr><tr><td>Nepal</td><td>₹10.92 Cr</td><td>36.75%</td></tr><tr><td>UAE</td><td>₹1.91 Cr</td><td>6.43%</td></tr><tr><td>New Zealand</td><td>₹1.14 Cr</td><td>3.84%</td></tr><tr><td>Bhutan / West Africa</td><td>₹0.56 Cr</td><td>1.89%</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
      <ul><li>At March 31, 2026, the book was ₹101.65 crore; commercial brewery equipment represented 88.39%.</li><li>Germany revenue equals the disclosed largest-customer revenue amount, but the RHP does not name the counterparty. The overlap should not be used to infer identity.</li><li>Export growth diversifies demand but adds execution, freight, FX, collection and country risks.</li><li>Order book is not guaranteed revenue: site readiness, scope changes and customer approvals can move recognition and collection.</li></ul>
      <div class="callout"><strong>Key question:</strong> What portion of the ₹81.30 crore book is executable in FY27, what advance has been collected, and what gross margin / working capital is embedded by project?</div>
    </section>

    <section id="capacity">
      <p class="section-kicker">Capacity—area is not output</p><h2>7. Manufacturing footprint and expansion</h2>
      <div class="image-row"><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Factory exterior"><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Malur factory interior"><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Jaipur factory exterior"></div>
      <div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Facility</th><th>Current built-up area</th><th>Post expansion</th><th>Change</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Bengaluru / Malur</td><td>13,789.77 sq. ft.</td><td>13,789.77 sq. ft.</td><td>No disclosed area addition</td></tr><tr><td>Jaipur / Chomu</td><td>19,424.98 sq. ft.</td><td>60,134.98 sq. ft.</td><td>+40,710 sq. ft.; 3.10x</td></tr><tr><td>Combined</td><td>33,214.75 sq. ft.</td><td>73,924.75 sq. ft.</td><td>+122.6%; 2.23x</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
      <h3>₹11.61 crore Jaipur capex</h3><div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Component</th><th>Amount</th><th>Purpose / machinery</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Civil work</td><td>₹1.66 Cr</td><td>Building and site civil works</td></tr><tr><td>Shed and roofing</td><td>₹3.85 Cr</td><td>40,710 sq. ft. additional built-up area</td></tr><tr><td>Machinery</td><td>₹6.10 Cr</td><td>TRUMPF dimple punching, AMADA 3 kW laser cutting, EOT cranes, hydra crane and radial drill</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
      <div class="callout red"><strong>Critical disclosure gap:</strong> the RHP does not disclose product-wise installed output capacity, vessel count, tonnage, machine hours, current utilisation, post-expansion output, revenue potential, asset turns or ramp-up. A 2.23x floor-area increase is not evidence of 2.23x production or revenue capacity.</div>
    </section>

    <section id="strategy">
      <p class="section-kicker">Growth plan</p><h2>8. Expansion execution and business strategy</h2>
      <div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Workstream</th><th>Planned window</th><th>Execution risk</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Civil works</td><td>Oct–Dec 2026</td><td>Site readiness, contractor execution and approvals</td></tr><tr><td>Shed / roofing</td><td>Jan–Mar 2027</td><td>Weather, fabrication and commissioning sequence</td></tr><tr><td>Machinery procurement / installation</td><td>Nov 2026–Feb 2027</td><td>Delivery, integration, training and trials</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
      <div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Strategic pillar</th><th>Management plan</th><th>What investors should demand</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Automation and throughput</td><td>Dimple punching, laser cutting, lifting and fabrication equipment</td><td>Cycle-time, labour-hour and defect reduction</td></tr><tr><td>Modular customisation</td><td>Configurable skids, common BOMs and reusable software blocks</td><td>Shorter design-to-FAT lead time and improved margin</td></tr><tr><td>Supply-chain resilience</td><td>Local / dual sourcing and procurement discipline</td><td>Imported-content trend and critical lead times</td></tr><tr><td>Lifecycle support</td><td>PM, remote diagnostics, training, spares, O&amp;M and AMC</td><td>Recurring-service revenue and installed-base metrics</td></tr><tr><td>Targeted exports</td><td>Key accounts and multi-site customer relationships</td><td>Win rate, country concentration and cash conversion</td></tr><tr><td>Environmental solutions</td><td>Paques-supported wastewater and biogas capability</td><td>Pipeline, economics and commercial terms</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
      <div class="callout amber"><strong>Approvals watch:</strong> consent to operate and factory licence have been obtained for Jaipur, but the fire NOC was pending. The Jaipur factory and registered office also lacked occupancy/completion certificates as disclosed in risk factors.</div>
      <p>The direction is coherent: standardise design, increase in-house fabrication, support larger projects and monetise the installed base. The missing bridge connects the machinery to incremental throughput, revenue, margins, working capital and ROCE.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="financials">
      <p class="section-kicker">Income statement</p><h2>11. Financial performance—FY26 was a step change</h2>
      <div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>₹ crore / margin</th><th>FY24</th><th>FY25</th><th>FY26</th><th>Trend</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Revenue from operations</td><td>88.96</td><td>75.17</td><td>101.16</td><td>6.6% CAGR; volatile</td></tr><tr><td>Gross profit</td><td>29.21</td><td>36.17</td><td>47.58</td><td>Margin expanded sharply</td></tr><tr><td>Gross margin</td><td>32.83%</td><td>48.12%</td><td>47.03%</td><td>FY26 sustained FY25 level</td></tr><tr><td>EBITDA</td><td>4.48</td><td>10.13</td><td>19.26</td><td>More than 4x FY24</td></tr><tr><td>EBITDA margin</td><td>5.03%</td><td>13.48%</td><td>19.04%</td><td>+1,401 bps versus FY24</td></tr><tr><td>PAT</td><td>2.00</td><td>4.91</td><td>11.56</td><td>Sharp operating leverage</td></tr><tr><td>PAT margin</td><td>2.25%</td><td>6.54%</td><td>11.42%</td><td>Strong improvement</td></tr><tr><td>ROCE</td><td>20.55%</td><td>31.92%</td><td>37.61%</td><td>Strong disclosed return</td></tr><tr><td>ROE</td><td>27.92%</td><td>46.14%</td><td>60.95%</td><td>Elevated by small equity base / leverage</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
      <div class="callout amber"><strong>Quality question:</strong> FY26 revenue grew 34.6%, but EBITDA grew 90.1%. The company must show that the 19% margin reflects durable project mix and execution gains—not a temporary concentration of high-margin milestones.</div>
      <h3>Peer caution</h3><p>The RHP presents only Praj Industries as a listed peer and explicitly says it is not strictly comparable. Praj is vastly larger with a broader technology portfolio; its point-in-time earnings and P/E are not a reliable anchor for this SME issue.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="cashflow">
      <p class="section-kicker">Earnings conversion</p><h2>12. Cash flow, leverage and working capital</h2>
      <div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Metric</th><th>FY24</th><th>FY25</th><th>FY26</th><th>Assessment</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Cash flow from operations</td><td>₹0.62 Cr</td><td>₹0.60 Cr</td><td>₹7.98 Cr</td><td>Improved materially in FY26</td></tr><tr><td>CFO / PAT</td><td>31.1%</td><td>12.3%</td><td>69.1%</td><td>Still below earnings</td></tr><tr><td>Receivable days</td><td>100</td><td>178</td><td>152</td><td>Elevated; approvals extend collection</td></tr><tr><td>Inventory days</td><td>38</td><td>48</td><td>46</td><td>Moderate but project-dependent</td></tr><tr><td>Payable days</td><td>173</td><td>193</td><td>235</td><td>Supplier funding increased</td></tr><tr><td>Net working capital</td><td>₹9.23 Cr</td><td>₹16.38 Cr</td><td>₹25.53 Cr</td><td>25.2% of FY26 revenue</td></tr><tr><td>Debt / equity</td><td>—</td><td>—</td><td>1.09x</td><td>Meaningful leverage pre-issue</td></tr><tr><td>DSCR</td><td>—</td><td>—</td><td>2.66x</td><td>Adequate at FY26 earnings</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
      <div class="stats"><div class="stat"><strong>49.8%</strong><span>Cumulative CFO / PAT</span></div><div class="stat"><strong>₹21.52 Cr</strong><span>FY26 net debt approx.</span></div><div class="stat"><strong>₹42.77 Cr</strong><span>FY26 receivables</span></div><div class="stat"><strong>₹25.35 Cr</strong><span>Short-term loans / advances</span></div></div>
      <ul><li>Cumulative CFO of ₹9.21 crore covered only about half of cumulative PAT of ₹18.48 crore.</li><li>FY26 debt was about ₹26.96 crore against cash of ₹5.44 crore; the IPO proposes ₹6.48 crore of repayment.</li><li>Payable days of 235 cushioned cash flow. Normalisation toward the FY27 assumption of 150 days could absorb liquidity.</li><li>FY27 estimated working capital rises to ₹63.95 crore; only ₹9.50 crore of IPO funds is earmarked for incremental working capital.</li></ul>
      <div class="callout red"><strong>Watch the cash, not only PAT:</strong> growth can consume cash through advances, inventory, milestone receivables and retention money well before revenue converts to collections.</div>
    </section>

      <div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Offer component</th><th>Shares</th><th>At ₹118</th><th>Use / seller</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Fresh issue</td><td>32.556 lakh</td><td>₹38.42 Cr</td><td>Jaipur capex ₹11 Cr; debt repayment ₹6.48 Cr; working capital ₹9.50 Cr; balance GCP / expenses</td></tr><tr><td>Offer for sale</td><td>3.480 lakh</td><td>₹4.11 Cr</td><td>A. L. Arun Kumar and Sailaja Arun Kumar: 1.740 lakh shares each</td></tr><tr><td>Total offer</td><td>36.036 lakh</td><td>₹42.52 Cr</td><td>27.00% of post-issue equity</td></tr></tbody></table></div>

      <div class="callout amber"><strong>Pre-IPO transaction:</strong> on September 9, 2026, promoter Arun Kumar sold 4.00 lakh shares to Convivial Advisors LLP at ₹118—the IPO cap price—representing 3% of post-issue capital. Investors should understand the rationale and any commercial relationship.</div>
      <p>At 13.6x post-money FY26 earnings, the headline multiple is not demanding. The risk is the denominator: FY26 EBITDA margin was a record 19% after a volatile revenue history, while cumulative cash conversion was only 50%.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="governance">
      <p class="section-kicker">Diligence flags</p><h2>15. Governance, related parties and compliance</h2>
      <div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Area</th><th>Disclosure</th><th>Assessment</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Independent directors</td><td>Appointed after threshold breach; compounding application pending</td><td>IPO-era remediation; test effectiveness after listing</td></tr><tr><td>Corporate records</td><td>ROC delays/discrepancies; some transfer forms and gift deeds untraceable and reconstructed</td><td>Historic control weakness</td></tr><tr><td>Deposits</td><td>Compounding fee of ₹75,000 paid; order dated 14 Feb 2026</td><td>Resolved but adds to compliance pattern</td></tr><tr><td>Statutory dues / loans</td><td>Multiple GST, PF/ESI and instalment delays</td><td>Liquidity and control discipline need monitoring</td></tr><tr><td>Properties / approvals</td><td>Occupancy/completion certificates absent for Jaipur factory and registered office; fire NOC pending</td><td>Potential operational / regulatory exposure</td></tr><tr><td>Tax matters</td><td>Proceedings ₹21.24 lakh; contingent tax liabilities ₹36.31 lakh</td><td>Not large relative to offer, but track outcomes</td></tr></tbody></table></div>

      <div class="callout red"><strong>Governance verdict:</strong> the issues are not individually thesis-breaking, but together show that public-company controls are newly installed. Clean filings, independent review of related parties and transparent capex reporting are essential post-listing tests.</div>
    </section>

    <section id="questions">
      <p class="section-kicker">Management checklist</p><h2>16. Questions management must answer</h2>
      <div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>#</th><th>Question</th><th>Why it matters</th></tr></thead><tbody>
        <tr><td>1</td><td>What are current and post-expansion product-wise capacities, utilisation, machine hours and bottlenecks?</td><td>Floor area is not output capacity.</td></tr><tr><td>2</td><td>What revenue, EBITDA, asset turns and ROCE does the Jaipur capex target?</td><td>The project lacks a financial bridge.</td></tr><tr><td>3</td><td>How much of the ₹81.30 crore order book is executable in FY27 and backed by advances?</td><td>Tests visibility and working-capital risk.</td></tr><tr><td>4</td><td>Who are the top customers, subject to consent, and what are customer-count churn, GRR and NRR?</td><td>Repeat-order revenue is not attrition.</td></tr><tr><td>5</td><td>Why did FY26 EBITDA margin reach 19%, and what portion is repeatable?</td><td>Valuation depends on earnings quality.</td></tr><tr><td>6</td><td>Why did cumulative CFO cover only 50% of PAT, and why were payable days 235?</td><td>Supplier credit supported cash conversion.</td></tr><tr><td>7</td><td>Which process designs, automation modules or vendor approvals are proprietary or exclusive?</td><td>Separates moat from capable fabrication.</td></tr><tr><td>8</td><td>What economics and exclusivity apply to the Paques collaboration?</td><td>Potential growth remains unquantified.</td></tr><tr><td>9</td><td>When will pending fire/occupancy approvals and the director compounding matter close?</td><td>Compliance should be complete.</td></tr><tr><td>10</td><td>What safeguards govern related-party labour charges, intercompany trade and advances?</td><td>Protects minority shareholders.</td></tr><tr><td>11</td><td>Why was a 3% post-issue stake sold pre-IPO at ₹118, and what is Convivial Advisors’ relationship?</td><td>Clarifies promoter liquidity and alignment.</td></tr><tr><td>12</td><td>How deep is the project-management bench beyond the founder?</td><td>Founder dependence is material.</td></tr>
      </tbody></table></div>
      <div class="callout"><strong>The most important answer:</strong> a project-by-project FY27 bridge from opening order book to revenue, gross margin, milestone receivables and cash collection—paired with a product-wise capacity table for expanded Jaipur.</div>
    </section>

    <section id="assessment">
      <p class="section-kicker">Investment view</p><h2>17. Final assessment and headline flags</h2>
      <div class="callout"><strong>Bottom line:</strong> SpectraA is a real engineering business with credible fabrication capability, reference installations, rising repeat-order revenue and attractive FY26 returns. The offer is not expensive on FY26 PAT. Yet the strongest year arrives just before listing, cash conversion trails earnings, customer identities are opaque, and the expansion measures square feet rather than output economics.</div>
      <div class="split"><div class="panel"><h3>Supporting the thesis</h3><ul><li>17-year engineering track record</li><li>End-to-end design-to-commissioning capability</li><li>₹81.3 crore order book</li><li>FY26 exports at 29.4% of revenue</li><li>Repeat-order revenue rose to 50.1%</li><li>19.0% EBITDA margin and 37.6% ROCE</li><li>13.6x post-money FY26 P/E</li></ul></div><div class="panel"><h3>Tempering the thesis</h3><ul><li>Customer names and true attrition not disclosed</li><li>Top-10 customers are 65.6% of revenue</li><li>No product-wise capacity or utilisation</li><li>Cumulative CFO / PAT only 49.8%</li><li>Payable days rose to 235</li><li>IPO-era compliance and board remediation</li><li>Moat is execution-led, not patent-led</li></ul></div></div>
      <h3>Trigger tracker</h3><div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Track</th><th>Bullish evidence</th><th>Warning sign</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Order conversion</td><td>FY27 execution with timely advances and collections</td><td>Scope slippage or receivable build</td></tr><tr><td>Capacity</td><td>Output/utilisation and customer-backed ramp disclosed</td><td>Only building-completion updates</td></tr><tr><td>Margins</td><td>Mid-to-high teens with steady cash conversion</td><td>Sharp normalisation after listing</td></tr><tr><td>Service moat</td><td>AMC/O&amp;M and repeat-project metrics expand</td><td>One-off fabrication remains dominant</td></tr><tr><td>Governance</td><td>Clean filings, approvals closed, disciplined RPTs</td><td>Fresh delays or unexplained balances</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
      <h3>Headline flags</h3><div class="flag-list">
        <div class="flag positive"><b>POSITIVE</b><span>End-to-end process-plant capability, ₹81.3 crore order book and rising export execution.</span></div>
        <div class="flag positive"><b>POSITIVE</b><span>FY26 EBITDA margin of 19.0%, PAT margin of 11.4% and ROCE of 37.6%.</span></div>
        <div class="flag watch"><b>WATCH</b><span>Top-10 customers contribute 65.6%; names and true attrition are not disclosed.</span></div>
        <div class="flag watch"><b>WATCH</b><span>The execution moat is credible, but no patent portfolio or exclusive core licence is disclosed.</span></div>
        <div class="flag risk"><b>RED FLAG</b><span>The 2.23x factory-area expansion has no disclosed product output, utilisation or revenue-capacity bridge.</span></div>
        <div class="flag risk"><b>RED FLAG</b><span>Cumulative CFO / PAT is 49.8% and FY26 payable days rose to 235.</span></div>
        <div class="flag risk"><b>GOVERNANCE</b><span>Historic compliance gaps and recent board/CFO/CS appointments make post-listing controls a key test.</span></div>
        <div class="flag valuation"><b>VALUATION</b><span>₹118 implies 13.6x post-money FY26 P/E—reasonable only if FY26 margins and cash conversion prove durable.</span></div>
      </div>
